ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Question: In the bridge rectifier filter circuit shown in figure, given \( u_2 = 10\sqrt{2} \sin(\omega t) \) V, if the load is open, the output voltage becomes ________V.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the attached figure is a transformer, and the secondary voltage is labeled u2; the secondary is connected to a bridge rectifier circuit composed of four diodes VD1, VD2, VD3, and VD4. The right side of the rectified output end is connected with a filter capacitor C, the capacitor is in parallel with the load RL, the output voltage uo is marked across the two ends of the load, with the upper end positive and the lower end negative. Reasoning: The problem gives u2 = 10√2 sin(ωt) V, therefore the peak value of the transformer secondary AC voltage is 10√2 V. In bridge rectification plus capacitor filtering, if the load is open-circuited, after the filter capacitor charges to the peak value of the rectified voltage, there is no load discharge path; treated according to ideal diodes, the output voltage remains at the secondary peak value. So Uo = 10√2 ≈ 14.1 V.

raw_record.question_text: Question: In the bridge rectifier filter circuit shown in figure, given \( u_2 = 10\sqrt{2} \sin(\omega t) \) V, if the load is open, the output voltage becomes ________V.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the bridge rectifier and the filter capacitor across the output/load. From the text, take u2 = 10√2 sin(ωt) V, so the secondary peak value is 10√2 V. Since the load is open, after the capacitor charges to the maximum rectified voltage it does not discharge through R_L. Therefore the output voltage is Uo = 10√2 ≈ 14.1 V.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：附图中左侧是变压器，次级电压标为 u2；次级接到由 VD1、VD2、VD3、VD4 四个二极管组成的桥式整流电路。整流输出端右侧接有滤波电容 C，电容与负载 RL 并联，输出电压 uo 标在负载两端，上端为正、下端为负。推理：题给 u2 = 10√2 sin(ωt) V，因此变压器次级交流电压的峰值为 10√2 V。桥式整流加电容滤波时，若负载开路，滤波电容充电到整流电压的峰值后没有负载放电通路；按理想二极管处理，输出电压保持为次级峰值。所以 Uo = 10√2 ≈ 14.1 V。

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram as a transformer secondary feeding a four-diode bridge rectifier, with capacitor C connected in parallel with the load/output terminals and the output polarity marked positive at the upper rail and negative at the lower rail. Also note the load branch is the right-hand resistor R_L, which is specified open in the text.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the given secondary voltage expression u2 = 10√2 sin(ωt) V and the condition that the load is open.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For an ideal bridge rectifier with a smoothing capacitor and open load, the capacitor charges through the conducting diode pair to the peak of the full-wave-rectified secondary voltage and has no load-discharge path, so the steady output equals the input peak, ignoring diode drops.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the capacitor filter is directly across the bridge output, and the load resistor branch is the output branch. Use the text condition 'load is open' to set load current to zero, so the capacitor-filter output holds the crest of the rectified secondary. From u2 = 10√2 sin(ωt), the crest is 10√2 V. Thus the open-load output voltage is about 14.1 V.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Open-circuit DC-equivalent/ripple argument: treats the final state as zero load current and no ripple, then selects the maximum available rectified voltage as the held output. Weakly distinct from the charging-path method because it uses a steady-state/no-ripple perspective rather than tracing charging intervals.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the figure as a bridge rectifier followed by a shunt capacitor filter at the output terminals, with R_L drawn in parallel with C and the measured output u_o across those same terminals.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the sinusoidal source specification to extract the amplitude 10√2 V and use the open-load condition to justify zero discharge/ripple.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: With R_L open, output current is zero; in an ideal capacitor-input rectifier the output ripple tends to zero because there is no discharge path. The no-load DC output is approximately the crest value of the AC secondary waveform, not the average value of the rectified sine.
